Wired through run_experiment.py:32 `ap.add_argument('--max-turns', type=int, default=30)` and run_experiment.py:53 `run_task(client, task, max_turns=args.max_turns)`. spec_features.evidence: harness.py:157-166: on `if not reply.tool_calls:` the harness appends a user message 'The test is still failing. Please keep working on it.' and `continue`s. The nudge text is really delivered and the loop continues. BUT the comment at harness.py:158 'nudge once, then stop if it keeps idling' is false in code: there is no idle counter or flag (grep for idle/nudge/count finds only the comment), so the same nudge fires on EVERY idle turn and the run is never stopped early on repeated idling — it is bounded only by max_turns. So the nudge is wired/executes but the claimed 'once / then stop' limiting behavior is not implemented.
spec_features.notes: The nudge is a prod to keep working (pressure), not itself a protective limiter; the only real bound is the separate turn cap. 'once' is not enforced — nudges repeat every idle turn.
